one_line: Speed up parallel LZ77 factorization with GLOBAL (absolute) match offsets; the suffix-array build is the dominant bottleneck (80-96% of time) and absolute offsets cost ~3 bytes/match hurting ratio. Find a faster and/or ratio-preserving factorization.

context.project: ACEAPEX — a parallel LZ77 codec whose ONE defining design choice is that back-references are stored as ABSOLUTE positions in the decompressed output (not relative sliding-window distances). This makes every block self-contained and enables block-parallel GPU/CPU decode and position-invariant random access. Decode side is already solved and fast (device-resident 221 GB/s on H100, bit-perfect). The ENCODE side is the open problem.
context.why_absolute_offsets: Relative offsets force sequential decode (position i depends on decoder state from i-1). Absolute offsets break that dependency, enabling parallel decode and random access. This is the project's unique value. It must be preserved.
context.decode_is_done: Not part of this task. Do not optimize decode.
context.hardware_available: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, CUDA 12.4; also multi-core CPU (AMD EPYC, 8+ cores, OpenMP).
context.must_stay_lossless: Reconstruction must be BIT-PERFECT (verified by byte-compare / FNV / md5 against original).

the_problem.goal: Given an input byte string T[0..n-1], produce an LZ77 factorization where each match is (absolute_source_position, length) and each literal is a byte, such that greedily copying from absolute_source_position reconstructs T exactly. Optimize for BOTH: (a) encode throughput (MB/s), and (b) compression ratio (n / encoded_size).
current_pipeline: 1. Build suffix array SA of T (currently the bottleneck).
3. For each position i, look at +/- W neighbors in rank order; among candidate source positions src<i, pick the one giving the longest common prefix. Emit (src, len) as ABSOLUTE offset.
4. Greedy: if best match length >= 4 emit match, else emit literal. Advance.

measured_facts_on_our_pod.dataset: enwik9 first 2,000,000 bytes (English text), also NA12878 fastq (genomic).
measured_facts_on_our_pod.full_SA_build_libsais_CPU: enwik9 2MB: ~39 ms (51 MB/s); fastq 2MB: ~25 ms (79 MB/s). libsais = linear-time induced sorting, single-thread.
measured_facts_on_our_pod.full_SA_build_naive_thrust_GPU: ~10 ms for 500KB = 47 MB/s FLOOR (thrust comparison-sort of suffixes, O(n log n * byte-compare), deliberately naive).
measured_facts_on_our_pod.SA_is_dominant: In Shun/Zhao parallel LZ77 (OpenMP, MIT DCC2013): suffix array = 0.631s of 0.788s total (80%) single-thread; parallelizes 5.3x on 8 threads. ANSV (candidate finding) = only 5% and parallelizes 7.6x. So SA build dominates on every platform.
measured_facts_on_our_pod.our_candidates_layer_parallelizes_well: On GPU our per-position candidate scan was only 3% of time (data-parallel, each position independent). On naive CPU single-thread it was 95% (not parallelized). It IS parallelizable.
measured_facts_on_our_pod.ratio_problem: With W=64 window on enwik9 2MB: coverage 97% but ratio only ~2.23. Absolute offsets cost 2.97 bytes/match (positions span whole file, need 3-byte varints). Delta-coding consecutive absolute offsets saved only 3.5% (offsets are scattered, no local correlation). So absolute offsets are inherently bulky, hurting ratio.
measured_facts_on_our_pod.reference_ratio: Shun/Zhao with a LOCAL window (max offset ~731 on same data) produced 240423 factors on 2MB (denser factorization). Their offsets are small (local) so cheaper to code, but they LOSE global matches and cannot decode in parallel.

the_core_tension: Absolute offsets = parallel decode + random access (our value) BUT bulky to encode (~3 bytes each) AND require a full suffix array to find global matches (the bottleneck). Local/relative offsets = cheap to code + smaller structures needed BUT sequential decode + lost global matches. We want the benefits of BOTH: keep absolute offsets (for parallel decode) while making encode fast and ratio competitive.
open_questions_we_could_not_crack: Q1: Can we AVOID building a full suffix array? Our candidate search only looks at +/-W neighbors in sorted order. Is a PARTIAL ordering (e.g. radix-sort by first k bytes, or an LCP-bounded structure) sufficient to find the same matches at much lower build cost? What k / structure preserves >95% of the coverage of a full SA?

Q2: Can absolute offsets be encoded cheaply WITHOUT losing their parallel-decode property? Delta-coding failed (3.5%). Is there a transform (e.g. reference-into-a-small-set-of-anchors, or a two-level offset = block_id + in_block_offset) that keeps offsets globally valid yet small?

Q3: What is the theoretically best encode throughput achievable on H100 for global LZ factorization at n=2MB..1GB, given SA build is memory-bound (GPU-SA literature says input sizes must stay low due to ~20n bytes memory)? Is block-splitting the input (build SA per block, factorize globally across blocks) a valid path, and what is the ratio cost of block boundaries?

Q4: Is there a fundamentally different match-finding structure (FM-index, BWT-based, hashing with global positions, minimizer-based) that yields ABSOLUTE-position matches faster than suffix-array, while staying bit-perfect and parallelizable?
hard_constraints: Matches MUST be absolute positions (not relative distances). This is non-negotiable — it is the project's identity.
Must be parallelizable (CPU multi-core or GPU) — no inherently sequential match-finding.
Must work on real data: English text (enwik9), genomic (fastq), binary (silesia). Not synthetic-only.
Prefer using or adapting EXISTING open libraries (libsais CPU-SA, libcubwt GPU-BWT/SA, Shun/Zhao Parallel-LZ77 ANSV+LPF) over inventing from scratch.

success_criteria.primary: Encode throughput on H100 significantly above the 47 MB/s naive floor (target: is 500+ MB/s or 1+ GB/s reachable? justify with measured or well-argued numbers), while staying bit-perfect.
success_criteria.secondary: Compression ratio competitive with local-window LZ (approach Shun/Zhao factor density) WHILE keeping offsets absolute. Quantify the ratio cost of globality.
success_criteria.deliverable: An algorithm description + reference implementation (CUDA and/or C++/OpenMP) that (1) builds whatever match structure it needs, (2) emits absolute-offset factorization, (3) reconstructs bit-perfect, (4) reports MB/s and ratio on enwik9-2MB and fastq-2MB. Plus a clear statement of which of Q1-Q4 it answers and which remain open.

what_we_already_ruled_out: Delta-coding of absolute offsets: only 3.5% saving, offsets too scattered.
Naive thrust suffix-sort: works, bit-perfect, but 47 MB/s floor (O(n log n * byte-compare)).
Assuming SA is not the bottleneck: measured false — SA dominates 80-96% everywhere.
Small window W=8 vs W=64: coverage 95%->97%, ratio 2.19->2.23 — window width is NOT the main ratio lever.
note_to_solver: We value HONESTY over optimism. If a path is memory-bound or ratio-lossy, say so with numbers. Negative results with clear measurement are valuable. Do not claim speedups without a bit-perfect check on real data. State assumptions explicitly.
